t: Count the Number of Vowel Strings in Range — Direct Counting
o: Count words with index in [left, right] whose first and last characters are both vowels ('a','e','i','o','u'). Example 1: "are" and "u" qualify → 2. Example 2: "aeo", "ooo", "artro" qualify → 3. Constraints are tiny (≤1000 words), so a straightforward scan is all that's needed.
k: A word qualifies iff both its first and last character belong to the vowel set — single-character words qualify when they themselves are vowels.

a.n: Approach 1: Linear scan with a vowel set
a.i: Iterate i from left to right, check word[i][0] and word[i][len−1] against the vowel set, and count. Nothing more is required at this input scale.
s: Increment the counter when both endpoints of words[i] are vowels.
a.t: O(total characters in range) — at most 1000 · 10 checks.

w: Trivial problem; the only subtle point is single-letter words (first == last character) and remembering 'y' is not a vowel here. A follow-up might ask for many queries over ranges — precompute a prefix-count array of vowel-string indicators for O(1) per query.
